**Hooke's Law:**
It states that within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to strain.
$$\sigma \propto \epsilon \implies \sigma = E \cdot \epsilon$$
where $\sigma$ is normal stress, $\epsilon$ is normal strain, and $E$ is Young's Modulus (Modulus of Elasticity).

**Stress-Strain Curve:**
```text
Stress (sigma)
  ^          Ultimate Strength (Su)
  |             _.-'*'-._  (Ductile)
  |          _.'         '.
  |  Yield  *               * Fracture (Buctile)
  |  (Y)   /                 \
  |       /                   * Fracture (Brittle)
  |      / 
  |     /  (Elastic Region)
  |    /
  +----------------------------> Strain (epsilon)
```
proTip: Clearly label the proportional limit, yield point, ultimate tensile strength (UTS), and breaking/fracture point on the diagram.
